newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan ends little changed vs dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan ends little changed vs dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed almost unchanged at 8.2963 on Friday from Thursday's 8.2962 against the U.S. dollar in Shanghai on cautious sentiment after fluctuations in the past few days, traders said.
The weighted average price on Thursday was 8.2964.
Dealers said the yuan moved steadily in a narrow range of 8.2960-8.2970 due to a cautious mood following fluctuations for the past few trading sessions.
The yuan opened down at an intraday low of 8.2968 and consolidated around 8.2965 for most of the session, hitting a sudden high of 8.2942 late in trading.
Trading was less active than Thursday with most done at about 8.2965, traders said.
One dealer said the yuan's wide movement earlier this week led to traders taking some care on Friday. "This sentiment caused it to stick in a narrow range." he said.
The "weekend factor" which makes traders more cautious was another factor, he said.
A second dealer said that even though the yuan had largely been in a downward trend in the recent short term, potential for heavy losses was limited.
"The fact that foreign banks have begun to do yuan business will boost the demand for the local currency and support levels in the short term," he said.
Dealers expected the yuan to stay at the current level early next week.
The yuan closed slightly down at 6.7015 from 6.7002 against 100 Japanese yen and unchanged at 1.0700 against the Hong Kong dollar.
The Industrial Bank of Japan and the Hongkong & Shanghai Banking Corp on Thursday became the first two foreign banks to do local currency business in China.
